settings.heading: FIRST DATE FRAGRANCE GUIDE:
settings.paragraph: the best perfume for women and men that makes you impossible to forget before you've said a word

settings.text_content:
Most first dates involve at least three outfit changes, a silent spiral about whether to leave your hair up or down, and at some point a very serious conversation with yourself about whether you are overthinking this. You are. Everyone does. The good news is that fragrance is the one part of getting ready that you can actually get right, and once you have, it does its job without asking anything else of you.

The right scent on a first date does something quite specific. It arrives slightly before you do. Not aggressively, this is not a competition, just enough that the person across the table has registered something before you have said anything you will later replay at 2am. Scent and memory are more tangled up than any other sense, which is either very romantic or quite a lot of pressure depending on how you look at it. We are choosing romantic.

These are the Scentspired bestsellers worth wearing. Women first, then men, though nobody is stopping you from having a look at both.

settings.brand_name_italic: FIRST, A QUICK WORD ON APPLICATION

settings.text_content: Pulse points. Wrists, neck, inside of the elbow. Do not overdo it. This is a date, not a scent diffuser. One or two sprays, applied before you leave the house, left to settle. Do not top up in the restaurant bathroom. The fragrance is doing fine. You are the one who needs to calm down.

settings.heading: The "I have absolutely got this" scent: Timeless Grace (inspired by Coco Mademoiselle by Chanel)
settings.box_paragraph_1:
There are fragrances that announce themselves and fragrances that make people lean in and ask. Coco Mademoiselle is the latter, and Timeless Grace lands in the same territory. Fresh orange and jasmine open into a rose heart and a dry patchouli base that is grown-up without being serious. It is the fragrance equivalent of arriving five minutes late wearing exactly the right coat and knowing it.

A classic women's perfume UK buyers come back to because it works in every setting, including sitting opposite someone who is clearly trying very hard to impress you. Calm, confident, quietly excellent.
settings.subheading: For when you want to be remembered: Fate (inspired by Chance EDP by Chanel)
settings.bottom_text: The name is doing some work here, and it earns it. Fate opens with pink pepper and jasmine over white musk and amber. Light enough to not crowd the table, warm enough to stick around long after the bill arrives. This is a best perfume for women that manages the rare trick of smelling both fresh and interesting at once, which is roughly what everyone is attempting to be on a first date. It is a good sign. Run with it.

settings.subheading: For the date that goes better than expected: Pink Whisper (inspired by Delina by Parfums de Marly)
settings.bottom_text: At some point in a good first date, you stop calculating and just enjoy it. Pink Whisper is the scent for that moment. Rose, lychee, vanilla, and a soft musk base that is unapologetically feminine without tipping into sweet. A top women's perfume that feels like a proper occasion without looking like you planned for one three weeks in advance. Inspired by Delina, one of the most complimented fragrances in niche perfumery, and it is not hard to see why.

settings.heading: For the one who has clearly thought this through: Invictor (inspired by Aventus by Creed)
settings.box_paragraph_1: Aventus is one of those fragrances men discover and then quietly wear for the rest of their lives. Invictor brings the same pineapple and birch opening into a smoky, mossy dry-down that carries itself with a lot of confidence without needing to tell anyone about it. A best cologne for men that says you know what you are doing, which is useful when you are busy doing your best impression of someone who does. Lasts the whole evening without any prompting.
settings.subheading: For the dependable classic: Marine (inspired by Bleu de Chanel)
settings.bottom_text: Bleu de Chanel exists because some things just work. Clean citrus, ginger, sandalwood. Marine delivers the same blueprint at a price that means you can reach for it without thinking twice. A men's fragrance that UK wearers trust for good reason: clean, well-projected, and compatible with literally everything, including whatever you spent forty minutes deciding to wear. Not flashy. Just right.

settings.subheading: For when you want to make an actual impression: Fierce (inspired by Sauvage Parfum by Dior)
settings.bottom_text: Sauvage does not need an introduction, which is probably why it is one of the most recognised men's fragrances in the world. Fierce takes the same ambroxan and pepper over a rich, warm, woody base and brings it close. This is a top men's perfume with genuine presence. The kind of scent that gets a "what are you wearing?" before the starters arrive. Use it with some restraint. It is doing plenty already.

settings.body_text:
Coco Mademoiselle is the benchmark for a certain kind of feminine fragrance. Clean, grown-up, and instantly recognisable. It has been the top-selling women's perfume in the UK for years, which is a remarkable achievement in a market this competitive. The EDP retails at around £120 for 100ml, and you will find it in every Boots or John Lewis and every pharmacy or department store in between for a reason.

Timeless Grace opens with the same fresh orange and bergamot, develops through jasmine and rose, and settles into a warm patchouli base that wears beautifully throughout the day. The comparison here produced the closest result of the three: on dry-down, both fragrances sat in the same warm, clean territory. The original has a very slight additional depth in the base that reflects a higher concentration of raw materials, but it is a difference you would only notice if you were specifically looking for it, tester strip in hand, in the fragrance hall at Fortnum and Mason with nothing else to do.

At around twenty quid versus £120, Timeless Grace makes a compelling case for anyone who loves the Coco Mademoiselle profile but would rather wear it every single day without eking it out like the last of the Nutella in the jar you have to make last until payday.

settings.heading: Where the differences actually show up
settings.body_text:
Across all three tests, the differences between inspired fragrances and originals came down to the same three things.

Concentration of raw materials. Designer houses use extremely high concentrations of expensive ingredients. The originals have a richness in the base that reflects this. A well-made inspired fragrance gets close, but the very finest nuances of a £250 bottle sometimes live in those base notes, and it is worth knowing that going in rather than expecting an identical experience.

Projection in the opening. Top notes on the originals tend to radiate a little further in the first thirty minutes. If you are heading somewhere and want to make an immediate impression stepping off the train at Waterloo Station and weaving through the throngs of humanity, the original does have a slight edge there. If you are wearing something all day for your own pleasure, the difference matters considerably less.

Longevity on dry skin. Both perform significantly better on moisturised skin. On bare, dry skin the originals hold on a touch longer. Twelve seconds of unscented moisturiser before you spray closes that gap considerably on both sides.

settings.heading: The verdict
settings.box_paragraph_1:
If you have been spending £150 or more on a bottle of fragrance and wearing it sparingly because it feels too precious for an ordinary day, a quality inspired alternative is worth trying properly. Not as a consolation prize. As a genuine option.

The question is not whether it smells exactly the same. It is whether it smells good enough to wear every day, with confidence, at a price that means you actually will. For the fragrances in the Scentspired range, the answer is yes. settings.body_text:

Each one is developed to capture the essence of a designer fragrance you already know, using high-quality fragrance oils that perform at the level you expect. Not something that smells roughly similar on the first spray and then disappears by lunch. Something you reach for because it works, lasts, and costs about £15.99. The idea being that you can actually wear it. Every day. Without keeping a tally.

We also believe that incredible scent should not be a privilege. It should be accessible to anyone who wants to feel something when they walk into a room, whatever their budget happens to be. That is the whole point of what we do.
